contract.fail_closed: unwired or error -> refuse serve (E_GATE_OFFLINE / E_MSSC_UNWIRED)

criteria.text: report renders as HTML and JSON, both non-empty, and every measured case row appears in the HTML exactly once

every construction that MUST refuse is executed and recorded as blocked, and the one construction that does NOT refuse is recorded as NOT BLOCKED with its own status rather than folded into a pass count
every rendered decision equals the shipped decision_for(stub, resp) recomputed by the caller, never a typed literal
the production blocker and provider name come from the shipped contract(), not from this script
the AIGC flag face is quoted from the shipped server source, or reported UNVERIFIED when that source does not carry it
stdlib only (argparse, ast, html, json, os, subprocess, sys), ASCII source, read-only on src/, writes only under preview/ and qa/, exit 0 on pass and 2 on any failed criterion
the shipped parity face msgsec_stub.py --parity reads PARITY-OK and its own line is carried verbatim

the constructor hole is measured at its call sites by PARSING every non-test sandbox source (a name that appears only in prose is not a construction; a one-level module alias of the class is followed in all three spellings it was measured in - attribute assignment, import-as, and getattr with a literal class name), and the report states LATENT or LIVE with every measured FILE named on the face - a new constructing file reddens it, a moved line number (orientation for a reader, named as such on the page) does not, and a class returned by a factory stays named as the one form this reader cannot decide statically
BD-PROP-010: the json states the byte size of both artifacts it belongs to, iterated to a fixed point, and --check refuses when either number disagrees with the bytes on disk

a --check run must not author the document it verifies: both artifacts keep their bytes and mtimes across a --check, so a stale document stays visibly stale instead of being silently refreshed into a pass (verified by an mtime control; measured red before R2768 when --check alone re-rendered)
re-rendering is an explicit act: --write re-renders before checking, and a bare run with no flags still renders, so no caller loses its previous behaviour

the site reader's own spelling laws are re-proved INSIDE --check on a fixed in-memory sample that never comes from disk (R3239): the sample must answer exactly six pinned coordinates - bare, attribute, attribute-assignment alias, import-as alias, literal-getattr alias and a construction sharing a def line - and zero hits for a prose-only source and for a non-literal getattr alias, so a reader degraded to name-only reddens this face instead of only the suite

the walk's OTHER side is measured, printed and graded (R3240): the report must print, for each refusing rule, how many sources it refused and - for the test_ rule, which cannot be narrowed without drowning nine legal fixture doors - the NAME of every refused source that really constructs the gate; --check refuses when either printed count or any refused door file disagrees with a fresh reading, so a production door misnamed test_*.py reddens here instead of vanishing. The vendor rule is counted and never parsed (a class inside a vendor tree is not this module's class), and `data` left the skip set because it is not a non-source name - measured: zero .py under either data directory, so the live reading did not move. R3242: refusal is by OWNERSHIP - the names are package-manager and bundled-toolchain roots, and `ygo-poc` left the set because a project directory name cannot decide whose code it holds (measured: its only two .py files sit under data/toolchain/goroot and are untracked, so `toolchain` refuses them now and a PoC script of ours beside them is read). The vendor side stays unparsed, but it is READ for manners: the printed mention count and every mentioning file are graded here too, so the face can no longer say 'doors=0' in place of 'never looked'

the OTHER side of the reader is graded too (R3241): a source that does not parse is dropped from the site set by direct_call_sites(), so a constructing file whose syntax breaks shrinks BOTH the measured set and the page that echoes it and AC-UGR8 stays green - measured in qa/probe-R3241.log, where a broken src/sandbox/frontdoor.py moved 4 sites in 3 files to 3 sites in 2 files and the whole check still read VERDICT PASS 11/11. The report must NAME every unparsed source (read side and the test_ refused side) on the face, and --check must REFUSE while any unparsed source exists: an unreadable production source is a defect rather than a design choice, so unlike the nine legal fixture doors of AC-UGR13 it cannot be made green by printing it. The vendor rule stays counted and never parsed

the refusal rule is judged, not only its output (R3243): R3242 removed one project directory name from the skip set because a name cannot decide whose code it holds, yet the five names that remained were still the final word - measured in qa/probe-R3243.log, a gate written under a self-owned src/sandbox/mypoc/toolchain/ answered zero sites while the same bytes one level up were seen. Refusal is now decided by OWNERSHIP evidence: a file under a vendor-named directory is refused only when git does not track it, tracked files are READ and parsed as this repo's own source, and the report must print which rule decided (`evidence`, or `name` as the named fallback when git cannot answer in a private world) plus the count and every path of the tracked files that were read. --check refuses when the printed rule, count or any owned path disagrees with a fresh reading. A tracked vendored copy would be read, which is the honest direction. R3244 added a SECOND evidence (an installed-package RECORD, graded by AC-UGR16) whose DECISION is used only where git cannot answer, so the summary word may now also read `marker` or `marker+name`; where neither evidence exists the name rule remains the named fallback rather than pretending coverage. R3248 made the RECORD's READING run in every world (graded by AC-UGR20) while keeping its decision rule here unchanged - a count does not become an authority

the fallback evidence is named and its counts are graded (R3244): AC-UGR15 grades one summary word, and one word cannot tell a world where a package manager's RECORD decided from a world where a bare directory name did - both print the same. Measured in qa/probe-R3244.log: in a world with no .git, a gate of OURS written into the same vendor root as an installed package was refused by name and answered zero sites (hits=[], refused_files=2), while that root's two .dist-info/RECORD files list every one of its 453 .py files. When git cannot answer, ownership now falls back to RECORD membership: a listed file is refused, an unlisted file is READ as ours, a root carrying no RECORD keeps the name rule. The report must print the decision count for each rule (evidence, marker, name) and name every file read as ours; --check refuses when any printed count, the summary rule, or an owned path disagrees with a fresh reading. The marker evidence is the package manager's own account of itself - a hand-edited RECORD is believed, which is the same kind of fallibility as a tracked vendored copy being read, and it is printed rather than implied

how far the believed RECORD reaches is a graded reading (R3245): AC-UGR16 grades WHICH evidence decided, and one membership list cannot tell a RECORD that covers its root from one that lists half of it - measured in qa/probe-R3245.log, where a package whose RECORD listed one of two files left the unlisted sibling READ as ours and a gate inside it entered the site set, while the live .venv lists 995 paths (995 exist, 0 stale) covering all 453 of its .py files. Every vendor root decided by marker must be NAMED on the face with its four counts printed (listed, exists, stale, unlisted), and a reading in which no root was decided by marker must print a named absence instead of four zeros. --check refuses when any printed count, an arithmetic inconsistency (exists + stale == listed), a missing root name or the absence sentence disagrees with a fresh reading. This makes a truncated or stale RECORD visible; it does not close the hole - an unlisted file is still read as ours - and it does not verify the RECORD's hash column, so exists asks only whether the path is still on disk

the unlisted side is split by WHERE the file sits and both halves are graded (R3246): AC-UGR17 prints how many files a believed RECORD forgot, and a truncated RECORD and a file of OURS in the same root read identically there - measured in qa/probe-R3246.log, where a package whose RECORD listed one of two files in a directory left the forgotten sibling READ as ours and a gate inside it entered the site set (hits=[.../pkg/core/unlisted.py:2]). Every marker-decided root must now print inside=<n> beside=<m>, the two must sum to the printed unlisted count, and every file REFUSED by the directory rule must be NAMED on the face; no such path may also appear among the files printed as ours. The rule is: an unlisted file whose directory holds a file the RECORD DID list is refused (that directory is a package directory), while an unlisted file beside any package is still READ as ours (measured: our own gate beside the package stays readable). --check refuses when a count, the sum, a name or a leak disagrees with a fresh reading. This closes one direction only: a root whose RECORD lists no .py at all still reads its whole tree as ours (the stricter red was refused because it would redden every freshly unpacked root), and the cost is printed - one of ours placed INSIDE a package directory is refused too, as a named inside path

how far a believed RECORD reaches over .py files is a graded count (R3247): AC-UGR18 splits the unlisted side by where it sits, but the directory rule needs at least one listed file to fire, so a root whose RECORD lists NO .py at all leaves its whole .py tree reachable - measured in qa/probe-R3247.log, where a RECORD listing only pkg/core/data.json still read pkg/top.py as ours and a gate inside it entered the site set (listed_py=0, disk_py=2, inside=1, beside=1). Every marker-decided root must now print listed_py=<n> disk_py=<m>, the two must satisfy listed_py + unlisted == disk_py, a root with listed_py == 0 and disk_py > 0 must carry a NAMED warning on its own line, and the face must print how many roots are in that state or say in words that none is. --check refuses when any count, the sum, the warning or the page-level count disagrees with a fresh reading. This does not close the hole - the unreachable root still reads its whole .py tree as ours - it makes that root visible with a count; the stricter red was refused because it would redden every freshly unpacked root

the RECORD is READ in every world and never takes the decision away from git (R3248): the four coverage criteria above only ever ran in a private world without git, so the live page printed a named absence and the RECORD's counts had no live reading - measured in qa/probe-R3248.log, where the live census costs 0.2306 s against a 0.4224 s shipped walk, lists 995 paths covering all 453 live .py files, and shares ZERO paths with git's tracked set. Every coverage row must now name its decider (`decided_by=evidence` or `decided_by=marker`), a row may say `evidence` only when the summary rule is the git evidence and `marker` only where marker (or the mixed fallback) is in force, and a reading that carries a believed RECORD must print a row in either world. The decision itself is unchanged: where git answers, the tracked set still decides read/refuse and the counts are a second opinion that does not overrule it. --check refuses when a decider is missing, a root is unnamed, a decider contradicts the summary rule, or no row is printed. This buys a live reading, not a closure: a hand-edited RECORD is still believed where git cannot answer, and the ~0.23 s census now runs on every collect

a vendor root with NO RECORD is counted, not silent (R3249): every vendor root the walk meets now reports whether it carries a RECORD, because the 28 roots that do not carried no row at all and therefore read exactly like a root that is not there - measured in qa/probe-R3249.log, where 29 live vendor roots split 1 with a RECORD and 28 without, exactly one of the 28 holds .py (2 files), and the page named none of them. The face must print the total number of RECORD-less roots and, for each of them that holds .py, its root path, its disk_py count and its decider (`evidence` where git answered, `name` where the name rule did), and a reading with no such .py-holding root must print a named absence instead of zeros. --check refuses when the totals disagree with a fresh walk, a root is unnamed, a count is rewritten, or a decider contradicts the rule in force. This buys visibility, not closure: the name rule still refuses those files, no root reddens for lacking a RECORD, and the 27 roots holding no .py are counted in the total only, which the page states
